results.author: Data Requests Officer
results.name: weed-zones
results.notes: This is a polygon spatial dataset displaying Weed Zones for weed species that have a declared class A or B zone that is not the entire Northern Territory or has a declared statutory weed management plan. Weed management zones are described as Class A, plants to be managed to eradication (eradication zone), and Class B, growth and spread to be contained (management zone). Both Class A and B are also described as Class C, not to be introduced to the NT.Information is provided for general guidance only. Map users should refer to the Gazette notice for the formal definitions of the zones. Weed species included in this dataset are athel pine, bellyache bush, brazillian pepper, chinee apple, dalbergia, gamba grass, grader grass, mesquite, mimosa, neem, prickly acacia, rubber bush and siam weed.

results.author: Data Requests Officer
results.name: classification-of-water-resources-top-end-and-arid-zone-climate-zones
results.notes:
This polygon spatial dataset defines the Top End region and Arid Zone regions as defined by the Northern Territory Water Allocation Planning Framework. The regions are also referred to as NT Water Resource Climate Zones.

The delineation uses the boundary between surface water catchments draining northwards into the Timor Sea or the Gulf of Carpentaria (Top End) and those flowing inland (Arid Zone). It is underpinned by a Top End index that draws from publicly available water balance indicators. These regions give an indication of the likelihood that a water resource will have the characteristics of a Top End or Arid Zone resource for guidance in water planning, management and regulation.

The zones are displayed in NR Maps - https://nrmaps.nt.gov.au/nrmaps.html --- See folder: Water > Water Resources. Layer name: Climate Zones.

results.name: nt-water-management-zones-wmz
results.notes: Water Management Zones (WMZ) are specific areas (with defined boundary) within a Water Allocation Plan Area established to manage the impact that may occur from underground water extraction. Rules for each zone are defined in a water allocation plans to determine how water can be used and/or traded.

results.author: Data Requests Officer
results.name: areas-permitted-to-clear-vegetation-on-unzoned-land-under-the-planning-act
results.notes: This polygon spatial dataset shows areas subject to all development permits issued by the consent authority (Minister for Infrastructure, Planning and Logistics or their delegate and predecessors) in accordance with the Planning Act for the purpose of clearing native vegetation on unzoned land since 2003 (when clearing controls were introduced).  (Unzoned land is land that is not zoned under the NT Planning Scheme - some zones also require consent to clear native vegetation.) Each polygon is subject to the conditions of the relevant permit.   Web link to a list of approved applications:   https://nt.gov.au/property/land-clearing/freehold-land/current-applications-and-approvals-for-freehold-land-clearing  The spatial dataset is provided for public access via NR Maps. Read Supplementary Information in this record: How to view this data in NR Maps.
